one_liner: Ecwid has a broad REST API (OAuth for public App Market apps, secret access tokens for single-store custom apps), but only stores on paid plans can call it. Developers can email API Support for a free paid-plan upgrade on a test store. Only third-party MCP servers exist.
auth_notes: Custom apps (single store) give a secret token, copied from the app Details page, that does not expire. The fetched pages show this API-key-style path. They also say multi-merchant distribution needs a public App Market app, which Ecwid validates. The pages don't describe the OAuth flow itself, so OAUTH2 for public apps rests on prior knowledge and is low-confidence.
access_notes: The API is only available to stores on a paid plan. Ecwid grants a free paid-plan upgrade to developers, but you must email API Support to get it, so it is not self-serve. Creating the custom app and tokens is free once the store is on a paid plan.
blocker_notes: A paid-plan store is required, both for a developer test store (free upgrade by emailing API Support) and for each customer's store. Extra scopes are a manual request to API Support. There is no test mode, so use a separate test store.

evidence.quote: Only stores on paid plans can access API
Ecwid grants a free upgrade to a paid plan for developers building a store customization
Access tokens do not expire and are tied to this one store.
Distributing to other Ecwid stores means a public App Market app, which does go through Ecwid app validation.
There is also no test mode in the Ecwid API
